chapter_theme: The five letters as the whole of religion. Sivayam is found inside the body (the root gate, the semen, the letter, the coil), the fire pit, the Rig Veda and the threads on the pot are asked what they are, the dancer of Thillai is the only god, and caste, alms and the distinction of you and I dissolve in the one body whose food, sleep and pleasure are the same for all. The jnani who is filled within and without has nothing left to think.
structure_note: No editorial order; the heading அறிவு நிலை is the editor's. The verses alternate between cipher readings of the body and the mantra (1264 to 1271, 1280 to 1283, 1285, 1286), confessions and assertions about the one Lord (1272 to 1274, 1277, 1279) and attacks on ritual, false gurus, caste and misplaced charity (1276, 1284, 1287, 1288). Most end on the refrain சிவாயமே or a cry of யாவர்காண வல்லரே.

1264.reading: Since the inner meaning of the Agamas is the undivided root, you, the Supreme, are held without thirst or enjoyment; setting the one foot, within the five letters that make known, it stood as the one enjoyment: Sivayam.
1264.nuance: அகண்டமூலம், the undivided root, is the claim: the Agamas reduce to one thing, and that thing is the five letters. ஏகபாதம் (one foot) and ஏகபோகம் (one enjoyment) are unexplained; tradition would take the foot as the Lord's single step or the one syllable, and the enjoyment as union.

1265.reading: Above the root gate a triple current; the mantra that rose in the middle of the four gates and the eight fingers; the form is one and becomes five; you who stand wandering here, I saw no difference: Sivayam grew.
1265.nuance: The sense turns on body-places and counts. மூலவாசல் is the root centre; முச்சரம் may be the three channels or three currents of breath; எண்விரல் (eight fingers) matches the breath-measures of Tirumular, where the breath goes out twelve fingers and eight return. The plain point is that the one form seen in all these is the five letters.

1266.reading: In the base of the semen, within the letter that whirled; at the base of the letter, you, the primal light, sat; at the base of the letter U, within the five letters that are known, becoming the letter itself it sat: Sivayam.
1266.nuance: சுக்கிலம் is semen, the bodily bindu of the Siddhars. அக்கரம் and உக்கரம் play on அ and உ, two of the three letters of Om, and on அக்கரம் meaning any letter. The verse makes the Lord a letter seated in the body's seed; the mechanics are the cipher's.

1267.reading: Within the coil, the Lord who cut within; the Dancer who destroyed thought in the sphere that was seen; the true substance that shines as the moon blossomed in the sky: the sphere I found and held is nothing but Sivayam.
1267.nuance: குண்டலம் may be the coiled power at the base, as tradition reads it, or simply an ear-ring or circle. மண்டலம் recurs three times with different senses (the sphere seen, the sphere where thought died, the sphere found). The moon in the sky is the yogic moon at the head on a coded reading, and the plain moon on another.

1268.reading: Five around and one chamber, a space beyond speech: you do not discern that it stands as Shakti and Siva. Shakti is your body; the Siva within is the wavering life. Madmen, you have not known the form in which the Lord stood.
1268.nuance: The five are the elements or the senses and the one chamber the body or heart; the verse does not say. The clearest line is the third: the body is Shakti and the life in it is Siva, so the Lord's form is the living person. பித்தர்காள் (madmen) is Sivavakkiyar's usual address to the unknowing.

1269.reading: Within the five letters where the mantra called the root sprouted, within the truth of the knowledge that the four Vedas recite on the tongue, because the one whose throat drank the poison, Hari and Brahma are there, the mantra one cries out is none but Sivayam.
1269.nuance: ஓலம் என்ற மந்திரம் is the mantra cried out, the cry for help; the verse says the only such cry is the five letters. The three gods are placed inside the mantra rather than the mantra addressed to them. Lines 2 and 3 return almost unchanged in 1373.

1270.reading: You who go off driving yourselves away with 'the tattvas': if the tattva is Siva, are you not the Supreme too? After setting the root foot in nada, which is the released life, know and realise the Father within yourselves.
1270.nuance: An argument from identity: if what you call the tattvas is Siva, you who are made of them are the Supreme. முத்திசீவன் நாதம் (nada, the released life) may be in apposition or a sequence; the syntax of line 3 is loose. The verse presses toward the identity of self and Lord that later Siddhars state outright.

1271.reading: Mulan who spoke the three for the three tens and three: jnanis who come and join, my head is at your pure feet; after setting it so, if you can recite so that the nature and the five letters appear, you will see the pure light.
1271.nuance: மூலனே is the vocative of Mulan, which is Tirumular's name; the verse seems to greet the Siddhars' parent, and the numbers (three tens and three, three) may be the thirty-six tattvas less three, the three thousand verses, or a cipher I cannot fix. Line 2's துய்யபாதம் என்தலை puts the speaker's head at the jnanis' feet.

1272.reading: In the heaven above, in the seven weights of worlds, in Nambar's own land, in the island called Naval: there is no god, none, none at all, but our Lord who dances in the hall at Thillai rich with mansions of red gold.
1272.nuance: A surprising verse from a poet who elsewhere mocks temples and images (999): the dancer of Thillai is named as the one god, with a threefold இல்லை. நாவலென்ற தீவு is Jambudvipa, the Indian continent; நம்பர்நாடு, the Lord's own land, may be Siva's heaven.

1273.reading: Becoming five in earth, four in water, three in fire, two in the fine wind and one in the sky, becoming natures that differ: who is able to see the rightness that stood as nothing but you?
1273.nuance: The counts five, four, three, two, one are, as tradition takes them, the qualities of the elements: earth has sound, touch, form, taste and smell, water four, fire three, wind two, space one. வேயிலாய (bamboo, hollow) is read here as the sky; the word is odd. The Lord is the one thing in all five, differently.

1274.reading: One in the ether, two in the moving wind, three in the red flame, four in the fine water, five in the fivefold earth: who is able to see the Lord who sat so, clearing maya in thought?
1274.nuance: The reverse of 1273, from space down to earth. தெளிந்த மாயை can be the maya that has cleared or the Lord cleared of maya, and the two readings differ on whether maya is the obstacle or the display. சிந்ததையில் is a misprint for சிந்தையில்.

1275.reading: If you can hold steady, free of the mind's modifications, the jewel-lamp that has no thought stands eternal; but if the Veda that everyone recites must babble within you, then what you saw in a dream is true: you have become clear, Sivayam.
1275.nuance: The second half can be read as irony, that taking the chanted Veda for the truth is taking a dream for real, or as a promise, that for the cleared mind even the dream is true. The first half is plain: the lamp without thought is the still mind, and it does not go out.

1276.reading: What is the fire pit you set up? What is the Rig Veda? What are the threads wound round the baked clay pot? What is it that clung to the light that sprang from the pillar standing firm, Pattanatha Pattar?
1276.nuance: Four ஏதடா in a row, addressed to a Brahmin priest by name or title (977 has சட்டநாத பட்டரே). The threads on the baked pot are the ritual kumbha. The light sprung from the pillar may be the Narasimha story, or the body as the pillar from which light rises; the challenge is what the rite has to do with that light.

1277.reading: As one leaf of the lotus that sprang up in water stands joined with the water yet is without water, see the quality of the learned Supreme that sprang up in the earth and stands joined with the earth.
1277.nuance: The lotus leaf unwetted by water is the stock image of being in the world without attachment. பண்டிதப் பராபரம், the learned Supreme, may be the Lord as knower in the world or the jnani who has become the Supreme; on the second reading the verse is about the sage's detachment.

1278.reading: What if they sleep, what if they wake, what if awareness goes and withdraws? What if the five fine senses go off in every direction? For jnanis who stand filled as the body fitted within and without, there is nothing at all to think.
1278.nuance: The jnani is not asked to control sleep, waking or the senses; they are made irrelevant. நிறைந்திருந்த (filled, full) is the condition: one who is the whole has no object left for thought. The repeated இலென் (what of it?) carries the tone.

1279.reading: The one letter that reciters recite is one; it is the body called Veda that proclaims this and nothing else; nada is one; the four-faced one, Vishnu and I are one: this is the rightness of my having realised the one that stood with nothing at all.
1279.nuance: ஓர்எழுத்து, the one letter, is Om on the usual reading, or சி. வேதம் என்ற தேகம் makes the body itself the Veda. The claim 'Brahma, Vishnu and I are one' is the strongest identity statement in the chapter; the syntax of line 2 is uncertain.

1280.reading: In the lotus space that swelled and held the axis, when it lodged and held, it becomes the great hollow of the element; when it moved within the fire, becoming forms and light, taking form upon the horn: that is the form in which the guru stood.
1280.nuance: Cipher throughout. புண்டரீக வெளி is a lotus centre, heart or crown; தாது is element or semen; கொம்பு (horn, branch) is a recurring word in Sivavakkiyam for a channel or the spine (1302, 1309, 1314, 1315, 1317). The guru's form is seen as light formed in the body. I cannot fix the sequence.

1281.reading: If you ask how those of earth and those of heaven came: nada and bindu mingled with earth as light does, the Lord and Shakti and the five elements, giving with earth and destroying; and so the seven are, even today.
1281.nuance: A cosmogony in one breath: nada and bindu, Siva and Shakti, the five elements make and unmake beings. The seven (ஏழும்) may be the seven worlds or seven births. The last line's grammar is loose.

1282.reading: The light that withdraws, the one who stood at the navel, the one at the middle place, the one who climbed up on the walking foot, the two who stand released, with the true and the false: know the Beginning that stood without beginning, standing near.
1282.nuance: A list of body-places and persons (navel, middle, foot) that tradition would map onto centres and breaths; the 'two who stand released' may be the sun and moon, the two channels, or prana and apana. The verse only names positions; who stands in them is not said.

1283.reading: You, the light hidden in the mantra that rose, in the letter that withdraws and in the reckoned sphere; after you have died within the reckoned sphere, within the laughing sphere Sivayam excelled.
1283.nuance: மரித்து, having died, within the sphere is the dying while alive of the yogi, as tradition reads it; the 'laughing sphere' (சிரித்த மண்டலம்) is unexplained, perhaps the state after that death. The three மண்டலம் of 1267 recur.

1284.reading: You did not bow with honour to the true guru who set you right. Madmen who hand out gurus, can you swim across holding that? The madman who hands out a guru and the disciple who came to take one both took the twelve beatings that cotton takes.
1284.nuance: குருக்கொடுக்கும் (giving a guru) is the trade of making gurus, and the verse damns giver and taker alike. பருத்திபட்ட பாடு, what cotton suffers, is a proverb for being beaten; the twelve may be its stages of working. The last line is 1207's last line in a new order.

1285.reading: The open eye praising, the sound of bindu and nada, passing beyond Meru and the cosmic sphere, in the space of Indra's magic where all the letters have perished: that you and I mingled there, of what nature is it, Lord?
1285.nuance: The union is placed beyond Meru (the spine, on the coded reading, or the world-mountain), beyond the cosmic egg, in a space where letters, that is mantra, no longer hold. இந்திரசாலம் is illusion-magic, so the space is itself called a trick. துதிக்கவும் (praising) may be corrupt.

1286.reading: After knowing 'Om namo' as the puppet within, after knowing it as the puppet within the thought of the sun-body: 'there is a you and an I', 'there is good lineage and all that'; realise within yourself that food and food are one.
1286.nuance: பாவை, the puppet or doll, is the life that moves the body (compare 1289's ஆடுகின்ற பாவை). Lines 3 and 4 read best as scorn: once the inner puppet is known, the talk of you and I and good caste (நலங்குலம்) comes to this, that all eat the same food. The sarcastic உண்டடா is the key to the tone; a straight reading is also possible.

1287.reading: When food is given to those who have conquered the five senses, does it rise to the Lord who stands as the good senses? Giving and bestowing on wanderers who have not conquered the five senses and roll in vanity is itself vanity.
1287.nuance: The gift is judged by the recipient's mastery, not his need; line 2 may be a question expecting yes, that food given to the sense-conquered reaches the Lord. வம்பர், the idle or wanton, are the pretended ascetics. The verse makes charity to the unworthy a waste, which the Kural's definition of giving does not.

1288.reading: Are the five senses, the nails that hold us, alike for all or not? Is the heavy suffering of being born from a womb alike or not? Idle men, you prattle; if you realise the truth, food, sleep and pleasure are alike for you and for me.
1288.nuance: The argument against caste from the body: the same senses, the same birth, the same needs. ஆணியான ஐம்புலன்கள் makes the senses nails that pin everyone alike. உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே, the same for you and me, puts the poet, presumably low-born, beside the hearer.

links.note: Both measure the breath in finger-breadths (எண்விரல், நால்விரல்) and end in the five letters: Tirumular's breath goes out twelve, eight return and four are lost, and gathered it is the mantra; Sivavakkiyar's mantra rises amid the four gates and eight fingers.
Sivavakkiyar makes the body Shakti and the life in it Siva, so the Lord's form is the living person; Tirumular makes the human body's shape the Sivalinga, Chidambaram and the dance itself.
Lines 2 and 3 of 1269 recur almost unchanged in 1373 (the four Vedas recited, the knowledge, the poison-throated one, Brahma and Vishnu); both resolve the gods and the Vedas into the five letters.
Sivavakkiyar fixes the one god as the dancer of the hall at Thillai, with a threefold 'no'; Tirumular widens the same dance: Chidambaram and the holy dance are everywhere Siva is.

Both count the Lord into the elements: 1231 piles up fives and threes and ones and asks who can see him, 1273 gives the qualities five to one from earth to sky and asks the same question in the same words.
1146 lists the fire pit, the four Vedas and the bound books and says all this ended as nothing when the poet knew the Lord; 1276 asks the priest what each of them is.
The Kural ranks one abstention from killing above a thousand oblation-pourings, leaving the rite its lesser merit; Sivavakkiyar takes the next step and asks what the fire pit is at all.
Tirumular's Siva-gnanis go about as the dead while senses and body remain; Sivavakkiyar's jnanis have nothing to think whether they sleep, wake or let the senses scatter.

Both set a single letter above all recitation: Tirumular says life can be won by one letter uttered without another, Sivavakkiyar that the one letter the reciters recite is one and that nada, the gods and he are one in it.
Tirumular derives the cosmos and the body's five elements from bindu as seed; Sivavakkiyar answers how beings of earth and heaven came with nada, bindu, Siva, Shakti and the five elements.

1207 says those who try to swim with a guru-given mantra, the guru-giving servant and the stubborn child, take the twelve beatings of cotton; 1284 repeats the proverb for the guru-maker and the disciple who takes him.
Tirumular's blind guru and blind disciple play a blind game and fall into the pit together; Sivavakkiyar's guru-giving madman and guru-taking disciple are beaten together like cotton.

The Kural defines giving as giving to those who have nothing, making need the whole criterion; Sivavakkiyar makes the recipient's conquest of the senses the criterion and calls gifts to the unmastered a waste. If the Kural's definition is taken strictly, the two cannot both hold.

The Kural says birth is alike for all living beings and only deeds distinguish; Sivavakkiyar grounds the same equality in the shared senses, the shared pain of birth and the shared food, sleep and pleasure.

1003 asks what a Paraiya woman and a Brahmin woman are, whether flesh, skin and bone are labelled and whether their pleasure differs; 1288 asks the same of the senses and the womb and answers that food, sleep and pleasure are the same for you and me.

source_issues: 1274 line 4 reads சிந்ததையில், a misprint for சிந்தையில்.
1284 line 4 is 1207's line 4 (பருத்திபட்ட பன்னிரண்டு பாடுதான் படுவரே) with the words reordered; the two verses are near-doublets.
1269 lines 2 and 3 recur almost word for word as 1373 lines 1 and 3.
1285 line 1 துதிக்கவும் may be corrupt; the sense of the line is unclear.
1273 line 3 வேயிலாய (bamboo) is odd for the sky; a variant may be lost.
